etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English triple (also þripell), from Latin triplus. Doublet of treble.

definitions.definition: Made up of three related elements, often matching
Of three times the quantity; treble.
Folded in three; composed of three layers.
(music) Of time, three times as fast as very fast.

quote.citation: c. 1601–1602 (date written), William Shakespeare, “Twelfe Night, or What You Will”, in Mr. William Shakespeares Comedies, Histories, & Tragedies […] (First Folio), London:  […]  Isaac Iaggard, and Ed[ward] Blount, published 1623, →OCLC, [Act V, scene i]:
quote.text: the third payes for all: the triples sir , is a good tripping measure

definitions.definition: Three times or thrice the number, amount, size, etc..
(informal) A drink with three portions of alcohol.
(curling) A takeout shot in which three stones are removed from play.
(mathematics, computing) A sequence of three elements or 3-tuple.
To become three times as large.
To serve or operate as (something), in addition to two other functions.

quote.citation: 1982 January, Popular Mechanics, Best tools for your electronics workbench, volume 157, number 1, page 106:
quote.text: Radio Shack's All-Purpose Crimper/Cutter ($9.95) doubles as a wire stripper and triples as a bolt cutter.

quote.citation: 2011, Mel LeCompte, The Tee Cotton Bowl:
quote.text: Examination rooms contain shelves overstuffed with football helmets, autographed equipment and even rugby gear. If the office doubles as a mini-museum, it also triples as a minichapel.

pronunciation: Received Pronunciation, General American, Canada, General Australian
